candidates.source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (Supplement to the Official Journal of the EU)
candidates.why_relevant: Canonical EU-level publication channel for contract notices and contract award notices above EU thresholds. Captures EU-institution and EU-funded contracts naming Ukraine, contracts of EU delegations/missions in Ukraine, and contracts where Ukrainian entities appear as tenderer/awardee — awards that frequently never appear in any Ukrainian national channel.
candidates.access_status: public, free, no login for search
candidates.legal_status: official EU publication; reuse permitted under EU open data / Publications Office reuse policy
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the official Search API (expert queries) rather than HTML scraping; filter by CPV (66xxxxxx financial/banking, 48xxxxxx software, 30xxxxxx equipment incl. banknote/ATM), by place-of-performance = Ukraine, and by free-text 'Ukraine'/'Ukrainian'.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball to developer docs
queries_used: TED tenders europa.eu Ukraine banking payment systems contract notice
"ted.europa.eu" API search Ukraine "financial services" award notice open data

candidates.source_name: TED Developer Docs — Search API
candidates.why_relevant: Documents the machine-readable route into TED: expert query language, field names, notice XML (eForms) bulk download. This is the difference between an ad-hoc lookup and a durable monitored feed for Ukraine-linked banking/payments contracts.
candidates.access_status: public; API key obtainable via TED Developer Portal (some endpoints keyless)
candidates.legal_status: official EU documentation; API terms of use apply
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled API pulls of eForms XML, stored raw, then parsed into a normalised award table.
queries_used: "ted.europa.eu" API search Ukraine "financial services" award notice open data

candidates.source_name: SIMAP / European Public Procurement legal bases (on TED)
candidates.why_relevant: Explains the publication obligation, thresholds and notice taxonomy that determine WHAT is guaranteed to appear in TED — essential for judging coverage completeness and for interpreting Ukraine's accession-driven alignment with EU directives.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off read; re-check annually for threshold/eForms changes.

candidates.source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA)
candidates.why_relevant: Single entry point for procurement run directly by Commission DGs, agencies and executive bodies, including DG NEAR technical assistance touching Ukraine's financial sector. Complements TED (many calls appear here with richer documentation than the OJ notice).

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Portal search filtered to 'Calls for tenders' with keyword Ukraine + financial/payment/banking; the portal also exposes JSON search endpoints usable for polling.

candidates.source_name: DG NEAR — Grants and Tenders (Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood)
candidates.why_relevant: DG NEAR is the contracting authority for most EU external assistance to Ukraine, including financial-sector and public finance management technical assistance. This page routes to the specific calls, frameworks and award publications.

negative_findings.description: No specific TED contract or award notice concerning Ukrainian banking/payment systems could be identified from search-engine results alone.
negative_findings.result_summary: General-web search surfaces TED as a platform but does not index individual TED notice pages well; notice-level discovery requires querying the TED Search API or Advanced Search directly with CPV and place-of-performance filters.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design for this cell must be API-first. A web-search-based collector would systematically miss the very notices the cell exists to capture.

negative_findings.description: TED itself has no Ukrainian interface language and Ukrainian-language search terms return almost no TED notice-level content.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Ukrainian query 'оголошення TED Україна фінансові послуги закупівля ЄС' returned only explanatory/portal pages (MFA mission guide, Prozorro Infobox), no notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ukrainian-language monitoring cannot substitute for English TED monitoring in this cell; conversely, Ukrainian terms are the right tool for finding the bridging/explainer sources and for Prozorro-side donor procurement.

negative_findings.description: No established Ukrainian-language shorthand was found for 'Ukrainian entity as awardee on a foreign/EU portal'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian sources speak of 'участь у публічних закупівлях ЄС' and 'ринок публічних закупівель ЄС' but there is no compact term equivalent to 'cross-border award', which weakens local-language querying for this specific angle.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language recall for cross-border awards is structurally limited; the reliable route is entity-name search (Ukrainian bank/PSP legal names and transliterations) against TED full text rather than concept search.

negative_findings.description: Ukraine Facility money is largely procured under Ukrainian national law via Prozorro, not via TED.
negative_findings.result_summary: Prozorro Infobox states procurement under the Ukraine Facility plan follows national legislation subject to the Framework Agreement; only EU-institution-contracted assistance goes through TED/Funding & Tenders Portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This bounds the cell: the largest EU-funded euro volumes are visible nationally, while TED holds the EU-institution slice. Both must be tracked or spend will be double-counted or missed.

negative_findings.description: No liveness or access check was performed on any URL in this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: All URLs are reported as discovered, with confidence scores; ECEPP notice-detail pages and DevelopmentAid records are known to sit behind registration/paywalls in part, but this was not confirmed by fetch.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must treat blocked=true flags here as hypotheses, and a 403 on ted.europa.eu or ecepp.ebrd.com should be read as bot-defence, not as a dead source.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumerated list yet of Ukrainian banks/PSPs and their exact EU-registration name variants and transliterations (e.g. NBU / Natsionalnyi Bank Ukrainy, PrivatBank / АТ КБ ПриватБанк, Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, UkrCard, EPS 'Prostir').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an entity alias table (Ukrainian legal name, EN transliteration, EDRPOU code, LEI) and run each alias as a TED full-text query for both buyer and awardee roles.

coverage_gaps.description: The CPV code set that best captures banking/payments/cash-handling contracts has not been fixed for this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define and pin a CPV list (66100000 banking and investment services, 66110000 banking services, 48xxxxxx software incl. 48480000, 30123600 coin-handling, 30144200 ticket/banknote machines, 79999xxx, 72xxxxxx IT services) and use it as the standing TED filter alongside free text.

coverage_gaps.description: Below-threshold notices on national portals of EU member states implementing Ukraine assistance (notably Estonia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany/GIZ) were not surveyed, yet implementers such as the Estonian e-Governance Academy contract there.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the Estonian (riigihanked), Lithuanian (CVP IS), and Polish national registers as a follow-up sub-cell, filtered on Ukraine-related project names.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm whether another coverage cell owns UN/World Bank; if not, extend this cell to UNGM and World Bank Procurement Notices filtered to Ukraine + financial sector.

coverage_gaps.description: Retention and back-catalogue depth of TED for expired Ukraine-linked notices, and whether award notices remain retrievable years later, was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test the TED bulk/open-data packages for a known older Ukraine-related award and measure retrieval depth before committing to TED as the historical system of record.

coverage_gaps.description: Only two Ukrainian-language queries were run; Ukrainian coverage of EU-level channels is inherently thin but was not exhausted.

brief: The EU-level notice landscape for Ukraine-linked banking and payments procurement rests on three primary pillars: TED (the legally mandated, English-language, API-accessible archive of above-threshold contract and award notices), the EU Funding & Tenders Portal together with DG NEAR's grants-and-tenders route for Commission-contracted technical assistance, and the EEAS/EUAM in-country channels that publish below-threshold delegation and mission procurement never seen in TED. A second, cross-border pillar sits alongside them: IFI portals — above all EBRD's ECEPP, plus EIB operations under the Ukraine Investment Framework — which carry financial-sector consultancy and bank-facing contracts under their own publication rules. The decisive structural boundary is that Ukraine Facility money is procured mostly under Ukrainian national law through Prozorro, so TED holds only the EU-institution slice and the two systems must be tracked jointly to avoid both gaps and double-counting. Practical collection must be API-first and entity-name-driven: general web search does not index notice-level TED pages, Ukrainian-language search reaches only the explanatory and bridging layer, and reliable recall of Ukrainian buyers or awardees will depend on a pinned CPV set plus an alias table of Ukrainian bank and PSP name transliterations.
